scenarioText: An abstract factory creates matching UI controls such as buttons, inputs, and dialogs for a light or dark theme.
An abstract factory creates a matching set of storage, queue, and compute clients for a selected cloud provider.
A game factory creates related assets such as terrain, enemies, and effects for a particular environment.
A document factory creates matching export handlers for PDF, HTML, and spreadsheet outputs.
An abstract factory creates a set of UI and system services tailored to a device family or platform.
An abstract factory creates a family of data ingestion, transformation, and persistence components for a selected pipeline.
An adapter translates a legacy payment API into the checkout service interface the app expects.
An adapter normalizes a third-party task payload into the app's internal task model.
An adapter converts incoming event payloads into the normalized analytics event shape used by the system.
A reporting layer reads from SQL, API, or file-based sources without changing the reporting logic.
A notification system sends the same message via email, SMS, or push without changing the sending flow.
A checkout flow routes payments through Stripe, Adyen, or PayPal while keeping the checkout API stable.
A document app prints to local, network, or cloud printers through interchangeable driver implementations.
A remote control triggers TVs, speakers, and streaming devices through interchangeable device implementations.
Shapes like circles and rectangles can be drawn on screens, canvases, or SVG backends without changing the shape logic.
A client assembles a complex API request step by step before sending it.
A reporting tool assembles a report with headers, body sections, charts, and footers.
A form workflow constructs a multi-step interface with fields, validation, and actions.
An application builds a runtime configuration object from many optional settings.
A document pipeline assembles invoices, contracts, or letters from reusable sections.
A game builds a character with name, class, and class-dependent stats step by step.
A food ordering flow assembles a pizza order with size, crust, toppings, and extras.
A password must pass through several validation rules before it is accepted.
A support ticket is routed through a chain of handlers until the right support level processes it.
An expense request passes through a chain of approvers based on amount and policy constraints.
A web request flows through logging, auth, rate limiting, and transformation handlers.
A message is routed through preference checks, channel selection, and fallback handlers.
A form submission is checked by sanitization, validation, and policy handlers before it is saved.
A text editor wraps insert operations in command objects so actions can be executed and later undone from command history.
A task runner stores commands in a queue so jobs can be submitted now and executed later by a worker.
A remote control binds buttons to command objects so the invoker can trigger different device actions without knowing device-specific APIs.
An admin console records actions like exports, notifications, and recalculations as commands that can run later.
A process engine models each step of a business flow as a command that can be invoked by a coordinator.
A productivity tool bundles multiple actions into one reusable macro that can run with a single trigger.
A file system treats files and folders through the same interface, allowing nested structures to be processed uniformly.
A menu system represents menu items and submenus together so the UI can render or invoke them the same way.
An organization chart uses a common component interface for employees and managers, allowing recursive traversal of the hierarchy.
A dashboard groups widgets and widget containers so layout and rendering can recurse through the same structure.
An access-control system nests roles and permission groups so aggregate permissions can be evaluated recursively.
A graphics engine represents shapes and containers in a scene graph so rendering and transforms can recurse through the hierarchy.
A notification service sends a message, while decorators add logging and retry behavior around the same send contract.
A basic HTTP client performs requests, while decorators add caching and metrics without changing the request interface.
A file storage component writes data, while decorators add compression and encryption as optional layers before persistence.
A text component can be wrapped with formatting decorators such as bold, italic, and underline without changing the original component.
A coffee order starts with a base drink and gains extra behavior and cost through decorators like milk, mocha, and whip.
A base notifier can be wrapped with email, SMS, or Slack decorators so one message is delivered through multiple channels.
A service wrapper layers logs, metrics, and tracing around one core operation so cross-cutting concerns stay separate.
A component can be wrapped with accessibility decorators that add labels, keyboard handling, or hints without changing the base UI.
A checkout facade exposes one placeOrder call while coordinating authentication, payment, inventory, and notification subsystems.
A video conversion facade wraps several media-processing steps behind a single convert method.
A home theater facade simplifies a multi-device startup sequence into one watchMovie operation.
An onboarding facade coordinates account creation, profile setup, email verification, and welcome messaging.
A report facade hides data collection, formatting, rendering, and delivery behind one generateReport method.
A device setup facade runs pairing, configuration, and health checks through one setupDevice operation.
A reporting workflow uses a factory method to choose the right exporter for PDF, CSV, or other output formats while keeping the export flow consistent.
A notification service delegates sender creation to channel-specific creators so email, SMS, and push delivery can vary without changing the notification workflow.
An application selects console, file, or remote logging transports through specialized factories so environments can change the concrete logger implementation cleanly.
A forest renderer shares tree type data across many individual tree instances to minimize memory usage.
A text editor reuses character style objects for many glyphs while storing only position and content-specific state separately.
A tile-based game reuses terrain definitions while each map tile stores only its coordinates and local effects.
An arithmetic expression is represented as a tree of terminal and non-terminal expressions and then evaluated.
A simple rules engine interprets boolean conditions against a context object.
A command string is parsed into operations that the interpreter can execute in order.
A playlist exposes songs one at a time through a custom iterator.
An iterator walks through pages of data without revealing how the pages are stored.
A tree is traversed in order without exposing the internal node structure.
Users send messages through a chat room mediator instead of talking to each other directly.
Aircraft coordinate landing and takeoff decisions through an air traffic control mediator.
Form controls communicate through a mediator that manages enabling, validation, and updates.
A text editor stores snapshots of its content so the user can undo changes.
A game stores save points so the player can restore progress later.
A multi-step form preserves draft state so it can be restored after navigation or interruption.
A stock subject notifies dashboards and alert services whenever the tracked price changes.
An order subject broadcasts status changes so email, warehouse, and analytics observers can react independently.
A publisher notifies multiple subscribers when a new article is published so apps and channels update automatically.
An editor clones a preconfigured document template to quickly create new reports with the same layout and styling.
A game system clones a base character prototype to produce variant enemies or allies with shared stats and equipment.
A commerce system clones a product configuration prototype to generate many similar catalog items with small differences.
An image viewer delays loading high-resolution images until they are actually displayed.
A secure resource proxy checks permissions before allowing sensitive operations.
A proxy wraps a remote service call so the client can interact with it like a local object.
A shared configuration object loads environment settings once and serves them throughout the application.
A logging service keeps one shared logger instance so every component writes to the same output pipeline.
A cache manager keeps one shared in-memory cache so all parts of the app reuse the same stored data.
An order changes behavior as it moves from pending to processing to shipped.
A traffic light changes its behavior based on whether it is red, yellow, or green.
A media player behaves differently when it is playing, paused, or stopped.
A checkout flow delegates payment behavior to a selected strategy so the order flow stays stable while payment methods vary.
An order service chooses a shipping algorithm based on delivery type without embedding pricing rules in one large conditional block.
A notification service picks a delivery channel strategy so the caller does not manage channel-specific branching logic.
Order processing follows the same high-level steps, but some validation and fulfillment details vary by order type.
Report generation uses the same flow, while each report type customizes data collection and formatting.
Data import follows a standard pipeline while different file formats customize parsing and validation.
Different shapes accept visitors that can render or measure them without changing the shape classes.
Shopping cart items accept visitors that calculate pricing and discounts across product types.
Document nodes accept visitors that export or inspect them without coupling those behaviors to the nodes themselves.
